messages:
jaime_support: Heads-up — ACME (private VPC) opened a support ticket: their app calls our hosted API fine but every request that triggers a KMS decrypt path returns a 403 from the KMS proxy. They also say audit events for those calls never show up in our collector. Escalating for security/compliance review.

benji_ops: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro and any error snippets? also any indication of network topology (NAT, proxy)?

jaime_support: repro steps from customer:
1) curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.private.acme.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
   => 200 OK (api layer)
2) service logs show downstream call to our KMS wrapper failing:
   "kms:Decrypt returned 403 AccessDenied: principal \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-service\" not authorized"
3) curl to KMS endpoint from their bastion fails: 
   curl -v https://kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1' --resolve kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:443:10.0.1.5
   => TLS handshake resets / ECONNRESET

Customer network: private VPC with default-deny egress, traffic flows through a proxy appliance (company-managed) -> NAT. They say they only opened 443 outbound to a small set of IPs (internal proxies), not to public KMS endpoints.

clara_sec: couple things to clarify: 1) 403 from KMS could be permission policy or network interference (TLS/SNI/certs). 2) Missing audit logs suggests our runtime couldn't reach the audit collector (egress blocked) or the collector couldn't ingest due to missing source IP. Need timestamps for the attempted KMS calls and the collector ingestion window.

jaime_support: timestamps attached (customer provided): 2026-03-17T14:22:05Z initial attempt, repeated at 14:22:15Z, 14:22:30Z. They also attached a pcap snippet showing repeated TLS ClientHello followed by TCP RST from proxy IP 10.0.2.1.

benji_ops: short-term mitigation we can ask customer to try before full review: allow outbound HTTPS to the regional KMS endpoints + our audit collector endpoints. Example security-group / iptables rules they can apply on the proxy: 

# allow KMS (us-east-1)
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 54.239.XX.XX --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# allow Redwood audit collector
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.200.YY.YY --dport 6514 -j ACCEPT

then test: curl -v --resolve kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:443:54.239.XX.XX https://kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/

clara_sec: also ask them to run these checks on the proxy to differentiate network vs IAM: 
- openssl s_client -connect kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:443 -servername kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
- tcpdump -w /tmp/kms-trace.pcap port 443 and tar/gzip the pcap
If TLS handshake succeeds from the proxy -> likely IAM/key policy. If it fails -> network/SNI/proxy rewriting.

jaime_support: customer says openssl s_client shows handshake fails unless they remove the proxy from the path. They confirmed the proxy is doing TLS termination for other hosts (internal) and does not have a passthrough rule for kms.*. That would break the AWS sigv4 flow and cause 403s.

clara_sec: important: KMS 403 could also be an explicit Deny in the key policy if the request's source IP or VPC endpoint doesn't match allowed principals. Ask for the key policy and IAM principal ARN our service uses. Run: 

aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-id> --policy 
# look for statements with Condition SourceIp or aws:SourceVpc/SourceVpce

please paste the policy (redact ARNs) — we need to confirm there isn't a conditional deny blocking their proxy IP.

jaime_support: they attached a redacted policy — no SourceIp conditions, principal includes our service role. So policy isn't the issue. Customer confirmed the proxy performs TLS intercept for outbound 443 by default, and we suspect it rewrites SNI. That will break AWS TLS endpoints and cause SigV4 mismatches, leading to 403.

benji_ops: recommend these next steps: 
- TEMP: request customer to add bypass rule on proxy for kms.* and our collector IPs (allow CONNECT:443 passthrough)
- Collect pcap from proxy to confirm SNI/ClientHello contents
- If they cannot bypass, recommend deploying a dedicated NAT with egress allowlist + non-intercepting path for Redwood endpoints

deploy-bot: ticket #ACME-457 linked and assigned to jaime_support, benji_ops. SLA: P1 (customer production).

clara_sec: compliance note: missing audit logs must be investigated for retention/completeness. Ask customer to provide: 
- pcap and proxy config (TLS intercept rules)
- timestamps of missing events
- confirmation if logs were forwarded to their SIEM (so they can correlate)
We need to confirm whether the collector ever received the request. If not, we treat as potential evidence gap and open a compliance incident.

jaime_support: booked a screenshare in 20m with ACME. I'm going to ask them to temporarily add a proxy bypass for kms and our collector IPs, capture the pcap, and try the curl test. I'll upload artifacts to the ticket.

benji_ops: I'll prepare a short doc for the customer with exact FQDNs and IP ranges to allow (include KMS regional endpoints, CloudHSM control plane, Redwood collector endpoints). Also include the minimal iptables rules and a test harness curl + python snippet to exercise decrypt path repeatedly.

clara_sec: once they confirm bypass and KMS calls succeed, we'll ask for replays of the audit logs (if available) and confirm retention window for the missing period. If the collector never saw the events, mark as data retention gap and escalate to compliance for record.

jaime_support: update after call: customer temporarily bypassed proxy for kms.* and ran the curl tests — KMS decrypt calls now succeed, our service logs show successful decrypts, and the collector started receiving events (14:45:02Z onward). They captured pcaps showing proxy rewriting SNI previously. They've agreed to apply a permanent passthrough rule for AWS control plane endpoints.

clara_sec: great — please attach the pcap and proxy config to the ticket. Action items: 
- jaime_support: attach artifacts + close P1 after compliance signoff
- benji_ops: send final how-to doc + recommended iptables/security-group snippets
- clara_sec: open compliance incident to document the gap and retention action items

jaime_support: will do. marking this thread resolved pending the compliance incident. :white_check_mark:
